title: Meet Kairos: Fifteen Players, Fifteen Champion Picks
subtitle: Ahead of the new season, Kairos's Main, Blue and White players share the champions and small details that say something about how they play.
summary: Riot meets all fifteen Kairos League players before the season for a quick introduction to their champion choices, offbeat habits and one passionately answered final question.

content.text: A new League program arrives with three lineups and fifteen different ideas about what makes a champion feel like your own. [[organization:kairos-esports|Kairos]] is preparing its Main roster for the LCS, Academy Blue for the NACL, and Academy White for development outside an official league position. Before the season turns every introduction into a stat line, Riot's production crew spent January 5 with the players at the Kairos campus. Each chose one champion to represent them and shared a detail most followers might not know. The result is part scouting shorthand, part group conversation, and a reminder that a roster is made of people long before it is made of match history.

The filming was deliberately small: portable lights, two cameras and ten minutes allotted to each player. The crew asked everyone the same two questions, then brought all three lineups together for one final prompt. After filming, players returned to their regular review schedules.
Kairos Main

For Main top laner [[player:noah-rkn-bennett|Noah "rkN" Bennett]], the answer was Fiora. Camille and Jax are familiar companions, but Fiora is the champion he would keep. "If I lose, I usually know what I did wrong. If I win, I also know what I did right. I like that." His review habit follows the same logic: he watches his own lanes without audio, to see whether a decision still makes sense without anyone explaining it afterward. Teammate 404 called the idea perturbing. rkN said it works.

Jungler [[player:ethan-vanta-walker|Ethan "Vanta" Walker]] went with Lee Sin, with Nidalee and Kindred close behind. He likes champions that can change the shape of a fight before it starts. Vanta also reconstructs the opposing jungler's route from memory before opening a replay, then checks whether his read was right. Thinkcard, listening from across the room, seemed pleased by that answer.

Mid laner [[player:mason-404-brooks|Mason "404" Brooks]] picked Orianna over a flashier option. "You can control a fight without being near it." Syndra and Azir round out his comfort picks. His collection of seven old mechanical keyboards drew a quick comparison with the younger White roster: some of the boards, he claimed, predate a few of them. 0bit was close enough to hear.

ADC [[player:liam-aster-oconnor|Liam "Aster" O'Connor]] answered Kai'Sa without hesitation: "You can play aggressive without having to play dumb." Xayah is another favorite. He also dislikes rewatching his own pentakills because, as he put it, there is always something ugly in the middle. 404 countered that collecting keyboards was an unusual standard for judging someone else's choices.

Support [[player:daniel-moss-reyes|Daniel "Moss" Reyes]] chose Thresh. "Basically everything he does depends on someone else doing something afterward." Braum and Rakan are close behind. For his lesser-known detail, Moss showed a small black notebook he has kept since before Kairos. It holds no full strategies, just names, habits and timings he has noticed among opposing supports. Aphromoo admitted Moss had one about him, so Moss closed the notebook.
Kairos Academy Blue

Blue top laner [[player:connor-mako-sullivan|Connor "SullCon" Sullivan]] chose Renekton because he likes a lane that starts early; Camille is close behind. His nickname is a straightforward squeeze of Sullivan and Connor, decided in roughly thirty seconds. Coach Hai's review: "You can tell."

Jungler [[player:jacob-xnox-price|Jacob "xNox" Price]] chose Nidalee: "If I'm playing well, it feels like I'm everywhere." Lee Sin is close behind. xNox built his first computer mostly from used parts at thirteen. Asked about the first motherboard, he declined to go into detail.

Mid laner [[player:owen-kite-hughes|Owen "Kite" Hughes]] chose Azir because, as he put it, "I like controlling space." Viktor and Taliyah are also favorites. Then came the answer that genuinely surprised his teammates: Kite has played piano since childhood. When Murmur asked whether there was a piano at the campus, Kite said he hoped not.

ADC [[player:tyler-murmur-grant|Tyler "Murmur" Grant]] picked Ezreal, a champion that lets you "do idiotic things and sometimes they look like genius." Jinx and Aphelios also show up often. His solo-queue habit surprised no one in the room: he talks to himself, since "I'm the only one always in the game." SullCon called that unfortunate.

Support [[player:lucas-grit-foster|Lucas "japalenogrits" Foster]] chose Rakan: "Get in fast, get out fast, and act like it was planned." Bard is another favorite. His nickname comes from a particularly bad personal experience involving jalapeÃ±os and grits. He would not add details, only confirming that the experience had been bad enough to deserve a handle.
Kairos Academy White

White top laner [[player:isaac-pebble-young|Isaac "Pebble" Young]] chose Ornn. "I can lose lane and still have work to do." Sion is another comfort pick. He carries a smooth stone in his backpack, a habit from before Kairos. Asked if it was superstition, Pebble thought for a moment: perhaps it was.

Jungler [[player:benjamin-vex-carter|Benjamin "vexemite" Carter]] went with Kindred: "I like having to decide how far something is worth going for." Vi is a frequent comfort pick. The name vexemite traces back to one taste of Vegemite, rated minus two out of ten. Pebble suggested trying it again to confirm. Benjamin saw no reason to confirm suffering.

Mid laner [[player:nathan-0bit-hall|Nathan "0bit" Hall]] chose Viktor because he likes a champion that "improves alongside the game." Orianna is second. His handheld console collection includes a Game Boy, a DS and a PSP, in varying states of repair. 404 tried to argue that seven old keyboards counted as a comparable collection. 0bit was not persuaded.

ADC [[player:cole-june-mercer|Cole "June" Mercer]] chose Jhin. "Four shots. That's enough." Caitlyn is his other comfort pick. The name June is exactly as literal as it sounds: he was born on June 2, used the month in his first online handle and never changed it.

Support [[player:ryan-luma-chen|Ryan "Luma" Chen]] closed the individual interviews with Bard, with Milio and Lulu also in his pool. Luma likes photographing city lights at night and has hundreds of pictures on his phone that he rarely posts. Asked why, he shrugged: "I took them because I wanted to see." For a moment, even the teammates who had been trading jokes let the answer sit.
One last question for all fifteen

The crew brought everyone back together for one unscripted question: which champion would you ban forever? The answers came nearly on top of one another. Malphite for rkN; Shaco for Vanta; Fizz for 404; Draven for Aster; Yuumi for Moss, prompting Aphromoo to point out that Daniel had chosen his coach. SullCon said Vayne top, xNox said Shaco, Kite said LeBlanc, Murmur said Yasuo, and japalenogrits said Pyke. White answered Illaoi from Pebble, Teemo from vexemite, Fizz from 0bit, Samira from June and Blitzcrank from Luma. Aphromoo called the session over. 404 still wanted to explain his Fizz vote. The explanation was postponed for review.
